column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/cd-stack.yml
# TAB-separated: <name> <context k=v;k=v> <expect-run csv> <expect-skip csv>
# WHAT THIS FILE PINS. cd-stack is three jobs on two independent string
# toggles: `deploy` (unconditional), `reconcile` (gated on
# `reconcile-after == 'true'`), and `notify` (gated on
# `always() && notify-slack == 'true'`). The rows below cross both toggles —
# off/off, on/off, off/on, on/on — because the two gates are independent and a
# single-axis table would let one arm rot behind the other. Both toggles
# default to "false", so the off/off row IS the shape every consumer that
# copies the README snippet gets.
# THE ROW THAT MATTERS MOST is `notify-without-reconcile`. `notify` declares
# `needs: [deploy, reconcile]`, so when `reconcile-after` is false its
# dependency SKIPS, and by GitHub's needs-propagation rule notify would skip
# with it — silently, on the exact input every default consumer uses. The only
# thing preventing that is the `always()` in notify's condition. That is
# load-bearing and invisible: delete `always() && ` and the workflow still
# parses, still lints, still goes green, and simply stops posting deploy
# outcomes for every consumer who did not also enable flux reconciliation.
# That row is the tripwire on it — it turns NOT-RUN the moment always() is
# dropped.
# THE `deploy` JOB IS UNCONDITIONAL AND STAYS THAT WAY. It is the job that
# actually mutates a cluster (`helm upgrade --install --wait`), and there is no
# dry-run / skip-deploy input to gate it — being called at all IS the intent to
# deploy. So there is no "don't-do-it" row for deploy: the honest assertion is
# that it selects in EVERY case, which all six rows below make. If someone
# later adds a gate to it, the first row to disagree names it.
# WHY THE `== 'true'` ROWS ARE NOT REDUNDANT. Both toggles are typed `string`,
# not `boolean`, so the caller can pass anything and GitHub will not object.
# `not-true-truthy` passes values that are TRUTHY to GitHub (`yes`, `1`) but
# are not the literal string `true`. Both jobs must stay skipped. That row
# pins the comparison as exact-string rather than truthiness — the difference
# only shows up when a consumer writes `reconcile-after: yes` and wonders why
# nothing reconciled, or (worse) when someone "fixes" the condition to a bare
# `inputs.reconcile-after` and every caller who passed `"false"` as a string
# starts force-converging production. `empty-toggles` covers the same axis from
# the other end: an expression that resolved to nothing (a caller interpolating
# an unset variable) must land on the off arm, not between the arms.
# WHAT THIS FILE CANNOT SEE — stated so its green is not read as broader.
#  1. FAILURE. The whole reason `notify` carries `always()` is to post an
#     outcome when `deploy` FAILED — the notify step formats
#     `needs.deploy.outputs.deployed == 'true' && 'deployed' || 'FAILED'`, so
#     the failure path is a designed, user-visible behaviour. This linter has
#     no failure state: a job is selected or it is not, and there is no way to
#     say "deploy ran and exited 1". So `always()` is asserted here only
#     against the SKIPPED-dependency half of its job, never the failed-
#     dependency half. Declaring `always()=false` to fake it would be a lie —
#     always() is true by definition, including on cancellation — so it is
#     declared `true` in every row and the second half is left uncovered
#     rather than faked.
#  2. THE SECRETS. `KUBECONFIG_B64` is deliberately `required: false` (see the
#     comment in the workflow), so a caller that inherits nothing still starts
#     every job — and `deploy` then fails at the `base64 -d` step. That is a
#     STEP-level outcome, below this tool's resolution entirely. "deploy ran"
#     here means the job was selected, never that a kubeconfig existed.
#  3. `runs-on`. `github.event.repository.private` appears three times in this
#     workflow and all three are in `runs-on` — they pick a billing label, not
#     a job. No `if:` reads privacy, so no job here can be privacy-skipped and
#     there is nothing honest to assert as one. Unlike auto-release-min's
#     table, the key is NOT declared as a tripwire here: this linter errors on
#     an undeclared path only when a condition READS it, so a declared-but-
#     unread key is inert, and the day someone gates a job on privacy the
#     undeclared-path ERROR fires on every row anyway — which is a louder
#     signal than a row quietly agreeing with its neighbour.
# The default shape: both toggles at their declared default. Deploy runs;
# nothing else does. Every consumer that copies the README snippet gets this.
default-deploy-only
# reconcile-after on, notify off. Proves the reconcile gate is load-bearing in
# the positive direction, and that turning it on does not drag notify in.
reconcile-only
# THE always() TRIPWIRE. notify's dependency `reconcile` is SKIPPED here, so
# needs-propagation would skip notify too if its condition did not call
# always(). Drop the `always() && ` and this row goes NOT-RUN — which is
# exactly the silent regression it exists to catch, since it fires on the
# DEFAULT reconcile setting and would therefore hit almost every consumer.
notify-without-reconcile
# Both toggles on: the full advertised pipeline, all three jobs selecting.
# The only row in which nothing is expected to skip.
full-pipeline
# Neither toggle resolved to anything — a caller interpolating an unset var, or
# an upstream step that produced no output. Distinct from the literal string
# "false" and must land on the same off arm rather than falling between arms.
empty-toggles
# THE CATCH-ALL. Values GitHub considers TRUTHY but which are not the literal
# string `true`. Both gates compare `== 'true'`, so both jobs must stay
# skipped. Red-flags any "simplification" of either condition to a bare
# truthiness test, which would flip every string-typed caller's meaning.
not-true-truthy
